article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning autoflowering hybrid
Genetics: Santa Maria × Cannabis ruderalis
Breeder: Paradise Seeds
THC Content: 10–12%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Sweet herbs, floral notes, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: 10–11 weeks from seed
Indoor Yield: 350 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 30–40 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Long before autoflowering marijuana became a major category in commercial seed catalogs, Paradise Seeds was experimenting with how ruderalis genetics could be made more useful to serious cannabis growers. Automaria emerged from that effort as the company’s first autoflowering variety, pairing the automatic flowering behavior of Cannabis ruderalis with the better resin production, potency, and flower quality of cultivated marijuana.

Historical material connects the line with the famous Santa Maria cultivar and describes the finished plant as compact, fast, resinous, and predominantly relaxing in character. Rather than competing with modern autoflowers for extreme THC numbers, Automaria occupies an important place in cannabis breeding history: it represents the period when breeders were learning how to transform ruderalis from an unusual botanical resource into practical, high-quality weed.
Genetics and Lineage

Paradise Seeds developed Automaria from Cannabis ruderalis and Santa Maria genetics. Period reporting that quoted the breeder directly identifies it as the company’s first autoflowering variety and specifically states that Santa Maria was involved in the cross. This is worth clarifying because information about the original Automaria is sometimes confused with Automaria II, a later Paradise Seeds development that moved the family in a more strongly sativa-oriented direction. The original plant was described as having pronounced indica characteristics despite its ruderalis contribution, while the second-generation version incorporated additional sativa influence and developed a more uplifting effect profile.

Ruderalis supplied the trait that made the project unusual. Instead of waiting for increasingly long nights to trigger flowering, Automaria begins reproductive growth largely according to age. Paradise Seeds described approximately two weeks of vegetative development before the plant moves rapidly into bloom. Once that transition occurs, lateral branching accelerates, pistil production increases dramatically, and the calyxes begin swelling beneath an increasingly visible layer of resin.

Santa Maria brought considerably more refinement to the equation. That Brazilian-associated cannabis line had a reputation for psychoactive quality and better flower characteristics than unselected ruderalis. Combining those traits gave Paradise Seeds a way to retain automatic flowering without accepting the weak potency and sparse flowers that characterized many primitive ruderalis hybrids . Automaria consequently became an early demonstration that autoflower genetics could produce legitimate recreational marijuana rather than merely novelty plants.
Effects and Experience

Automaria’s experience is considerably calmer than the energetic effect associated with its later Automaria II relative. The original cultivar leans toward a traditional indica-style stone, beginning with a mild mental easing before spreading into the body. Tension tends to soften rather than disappear abruptly, while the mind remains sufficiently functional for conversation, music, casual entertainment, or an undemanding afternoon. A detailed cultivation report described the outdoor crop as producing a pleasant indica stone that was relaxing without completely overwhelming the consumer.

At moderate amounts, that restraint is part of the strain’s appeal. Automaria does not need to produce exceptionally high THC numbers to create a noticeable shift in mood and physical comfort. The breeder-era potency figure of roughly 10–12% THC looks modest beside today’s 20–30% cannabis, yet the finished flowers were still described as surprisingly effective. Indoor-grown examples in one documented test even appeared stronger to the grower than the stated THC percentage would suggest.

The experience is therefore better understood as relaxed and uncomplicated rather than weak. Larger servings deepen the physical stone and may encourage inactivity, while smaller amounts can remain compatible with daytime relaxation. Consumers accustomed to extremely potent modern weed may find the transition gentler, but beginners should still approach THC according to personal tolerance rather than assuming that a lower laboratory number eliminates the possibility of discomfort.
Medical Benefits

A moderate cannabinoid profile combined with physical relaxation may make Automaria attractive to medical marijuana consumers who prefer a less forceful psychoactive experience. The cultivar’s traditional effects could be useful for temporary stress, muscular tension, minor discomfort, or difficulty settling down after an active day. Because the stone does not necessarily become heavily incapacitating at modest doses, some consumers may find it easier to manage than much stronger indica-dominant cannabis.

That reputation should not be mistaken for strain-specific medical evidence. Automaria has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials as a treatment for anxiety, chronic pain, insomnia, depression, or other medical conditions. Even plants grown from the same seed line can differ in THC concentration and aromatic chemistry, which makes broad therapeutic promises inappropriate.

Its historical 10–12% THC range may nevertheless be relevant for people deliberately seeking marijuana with moderate potency. Contemporary cannabis breeding has pushed THC concentrations far higher, leaving fewer options for consumers who want noticeable effects without maximum intensity. Actual cannabinoid testing remains important whenever Automaria flower is being considered for medical use.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Automaria develops a fragrance that is much more old-school than candy-like. During flowering, plants have been documented producing a sweet and spicy herbal aroma that becomes increasingly obvious as resin accumulates. Fresh vegetation and earth sit underneath that sweetness, while mature flowers can reveal a soft floral character that separates the strain from sharper Skunk or fuel-dominant marijuana strains .

Smoking or vaporizing the cured weed brings the herbal side forward first. Sweet plant material and mild spice are followed by floral tones, earth, and a slightly sharper outdoor character in sun-grown flowers. One comparison between indoor and outdoor harvests found both versions broadly sweet and spicy, although the outdoor crop carried a more astringent, naturally herbal finish.

No authoritative laboratory terpene profile from the original Paradise Seeds release appears to have been published. For that reason, specific claims about dominant myrcene, limonene, caryophyllene, or other terpenes should be treated cautiously. The documented sweet, spicy, herbal, and floral aroma provides a much firmer description of Automaria than assigning an unverified terpene percentage to the cultivar.
Growing Information

Ease of cultivation was one of Automaria’s original selling points. Ruderalis genetics remove the need to switch from a vegetative light schedule to a 12-hour flowering cycle, allowing indoor growers to maintain long daily light periods from germination through harvest. Paradise Seeds described approximately 14 days of vegetative growth followed by a vigorous flowering period lasting roughly 56–60 days. Branching increases noticeably once flowering begins, and mature flowers develop a high calyx-to-leaf ratio with dense resin coverage.

Height remains manageable compared with conventional photoperiod cannabis. In a documented indoor grow, plants finished around 80–100 centimeters, while an outdoor trial produced individuals approximately 60–75 centimeters tall. Indoor flowers became extremely firm and resinous toward the end of bloom, and three test plants collectively produced 102 grams. The same grow report documented approximately 30–40 grams per outdoor plant. Paradise Seeds promoted an average yield near 350 grams under suitable indoor conditions, although container size, lighting, nutrition, phenotype, and grower skill naturally influence final production.

Outdoors, the automatic flowering trait creates possibilities that conventional marijuana cannot easily match. Plants can be started once temperatures are reliably warm and harvested without waiting for autumn’s natural reduction in daylight. In climates with long summers, more than one crop may be possible during the same season. Because the complete cycle is short, avoiding early root stress is important; an autoflower has little time to recover from transplant shock, nutrient burn, overwatering, or severe training before flowering advances.
FAQ
Is Automaria an autoflowering strain?

Yes. Automaria was the first autoflowering cannabis variety released by Paradise Seeds. Its ruderalis ancestry causes flowering to begin according to plant maturity rather than requiring a traditional reduction in daylight hours.
What are the genetics of Automaria?

Historical Paradise Seeds information connects Automaria with Cannabis ruderalis and Santa Maria genetics. The original variety should not be confused with Automaria II, the later, more sativa-oriented development of the line.
How much THC does Automaria have?
Paradise Seeds historically placed the original strain at approximately 10–12% THC. Actual potency can vary with phenotype, environment, lighting, harvest maturity, and curing.
How long does Automaria take to grow?

The original breeder description indicates approximately two weeks of vegetative growth followed by around 56–60 days of flowering. Documented plants have finished within roughly ten to eleven weeks from germination depending on growing conditions.
What is the difference between Automaria and Automaria II?

Automaria is the earlier, more indica-like Paradise Seeds autoflower associated with Santa Maria and ruderalis genetics. Automaria II was subsequently developed toward a more sativa-dominant expression, producing a fruitier profile and a noticeably more uplifting, energetic high.
Final Thoughts on Automaria

Automaria is most interesting when viewed in the context of autoflowering cannabis history. Paradise Seeds created it at a time when ruderalis hybrids still carried a reputation for weak flowers and mediocre smoking quality. By incorporating Santa Maria genetics and selecting for better resin production, density, yield, and potency, the breeder produced a small weed plant capable of flowering automatically while delivering an unmistakably relaxing cannabis experience.

Today’s autoflowers can surpass Automaria in raw potency and production, but that does not diminish the cultivar’s significance. Its compact dimensions, straightforward cultivation, rapid life cycle, sweet-spicy floral character, and manageable stone helped demonstrate what autoflowering marijuana could become. For enthusiasts interested in the development of modern automatic genetics, Automaria represents an important early bridge between wild ruderalis traits and the increasingly sophisticated autoflower cultivars that followed.
